claims.claim: Amphilochius was bishop of Iconium (modern Konya, Turkey) in the last quarter of the fourth century.
Amphilochius was born circa 339 or 340 and died probably some time between 394 and 403.
Amphilochius was a first cousin of Gregory of Nazianzus.
The treatise Contra haereticos survives in a single 13th-century manuscript, Scorialensis gr. 137 (T.I.17).
The beginning and end of the treatise are missing, so its original title and author are unknown.
Gerhard Ficker argued in his 1906 publication Amphilochiana that the author was Amphilochius.
Cornelius Datema published an updated Greek edition in 1978 and entitled the work Contra Haereticos.
The treatise is directed against the beliefs and practices of the Encratites and Apotactites of rural Lycaonia.
The work seems to be written in the second half of the 370s.
The single extant manuscript has significant damage at points, requiring restoration and speculation by its editors.
